title: Modi Tells Indians to Skip Foreign Holidays as Forex Reserves Face Pressure
excerpt: With India's overseas travel spending at $15.3 billion and oil prices spiking past $104, the Prime Minister urges citizens to vacation domestically and cut gold purchases for a year.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has made an unusual public appeal: stay home this summer. Speaking at the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav celebrations, Modi urged Indians to avoid discretionary foreign travel, skip destination weddings abroad, and halt gold purchases for a year — a package of austerity measures aimed at plugging the drain on India's foreign exchange reserves.

**The Forex Math:** India's overseas travel spending hit $15.34 billion in FY26, according to RBI data, though that figure actually fell 3.1 percent year-on-year even before Modi's appeal. The bigger concern is gold: India imports roughly $72 billion worth annually, all paid in US dollars, straining forex reserves that stand at approximately $691 billion. With crude oil breaching $104 a barrel amid the US-Iran conflict, every dollar saved matters. Finance ministry estimates suggest a 30-50 percent reduction in gold imports alone could conserve $20-25 billion.

**Market Fallout:** The appeal sent immediate ripples through Indian markets. IndiGo's parent company InterGlobe Aviation dropped 4 percent on May 11 as investors priced in reduced international travel demand. Air India has already cut nearly 100 international flights citing airspace restrictions and soaring fuel costs. The broader Sensex has shed 2,700 points over two sessions as the oil spike rattles sentiment.

**Industry Response:** Top industrialists have publicly backed the measures, framing them as patriotic duty during a period of global instability. The tourism industry, however, is split — outbound operators face cancellations while domestic circuits from Rajasthan to Kerala report a surge in summer bookings.

**The Diaspora Dimension:** For the 4.4 million Indian-Americans, many of whom plan annual trips to India, the calculus cuts both ways. A weaker rupee makes India visits cheaper in dollar terms, but Modi's broader message — reduce conspicuous consumption, prioritize national resilience — resonates in NRI WhatsApp groups where families are already anxious about the rupee's crash to 95.63 against the dollar. The appeal also affects NRI property investors watching the economic headwinds closely.

**What to Watch:** Whether the voluntary measures translate into actual spending reduction will become clear in Q1 FY27 data. If oil prices remain elevated and the rupee continues sliding, formal capital controls — not seen since 2013 — could return to the policy conversation.
nri_angle: NRIs planning annual India trips face a complex picture: a weaker rupee makes visits cheaper, but Modi's austerity message and the rupee's crash to 95.63 are raising anxiety among families with property investments and remittance obligations in India.
author: Diaspora Desk
